rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation aggressiveness while respecting the hot FP loops that dominate this mandelbrot/whetstone-style benchmark. FLA and BCF get the highest SecurityGain weights because control-flow flattening plus bogus control flow are the strongest deterrents against static analysis of the core mandel/emit loops, and the tiny text section (~1.2 KB) makes their size bloat nearly free (SizeCost kept at 0.10-0.15). Their RuntimeCost weights stay moderate (0.40-0.45) rather than low so the selector still hesitates on the innermost float-intensive loops where branch overhead compounds. SUB is weighted toward DiversityGain with negligible cost/risk weights since it is cheap, safe, and composes with everything else. SPLIT is enabled mainly for diversity, amplifying FLA's dispatcher scatter at near-zero cost. IBR keeps the highest RuntimeCost weight (0.55) because indirect branching taxes hot basic blocks most, letting it apply to colder regions while protecting the FP kernels; its CorrectnessRisk weight guards the computed-jump edges in the flattened CFG. ICALL stays moderate since this benchmark has few call sites (mostly __muldc3 helper use) so its upside is limited but harmless. IGV targets the image/output globals with a mild CorrectnessRisk guard to preserve FP conversion semantics. Overall: aggressive control-flow obfuscation, cheap transformations applied broadly, expensive-per-branch transformations throttled by runtime cost.
